_meta.purpose: Catalog of 1RM estimation formulas and the %1RM model used by the IntensityModule. Epley is the Atlas default — consistent with analytics.js inline usage.

formulas.notes: Most widely cited in training literature. Slightly overestimates at high rep counts (>12). Already used throughout analytics.js for e1RM trend tracking — this config makes that usage explicit.
More accurate at low rep counts (1–5). Breaks down as reps approach 37 (mathematical asymptote); implementation clamps reps to 36. Use when the training log contains predominantly 1–5 rep sets.
Tends to underestimate at low rep counts. Included for completeness. Not recommended for Atlas prescription targets.

percent_1rm_model.description: Atlas derives %1RM from the Epley formula rather than a practitioner lookup table. For a set of R reps performed at RIR rir, the lifter could complete R+rir reps to failure, so: %1RM = 1 / (1 + (R + rir) / 30). This keeps %1RM calculations internally consistent with the e1RM estimate and avoids encoding population-level RPE table variance.
percent_1rm_model.rpe_rir_relationship: RPE = 10 − RIR  (Atlas logs RIR; RPE is the derived form)
percent_1rm_model.notes: Practitioner lookup tables (e.g. Tuchscherer/RTS) list slightly different %1RM values at the extremes. Use the formula for prescription targets and relative comparisons, not as an absolute %1RM assertion.

provenance.notes: Epley-derived %1RM approximation is internally consistent but diverges from empirical practitioner tables at very low rep counts. Flagged contested so the LLM conveys appropriate uncertainty when discussing %1RM.
